results.question: How do broken-promise rates change with the number of previously broken promises?
results.got: The broken-promise rate increases significantly with each additional previously broken promise. Customers with no prior broken promises break their commitment 40.1% of the time, whereas those with 3 prior broken promises break their commitment 69.3% of the time. [table: 4 rows]
sql:
SELECT least(p.prior_broken_ptp_count, 3) AS prior_broken_promises, count(*) FILTER (WHERE p.ptp_status = 'broken') AS numerator, count(*) AS denominator, CAST(count(*) FILTER (WHERE p.ptp_status = 'broken') AS DOUBLE) / nullif(count(*), 0) AS value
FROM l2.promises_to_pay p LEFT JOIN l2.collections_cases c ON c.case_id = p.case_id LEFT JOIN l2.agents ag ON ag.agent_id = p.agent_id
WHERE CAST(p.ptp_due_date AS DATE) BETWEEN DATE '1900-01-01' AND DATE '2999-12-31'
  AND p.ptp_status IN ('kept', 'partially_kept', 'broken')
GROUP BY ALL
ORDER BY value DESC NULLS LAST, prior_broken_promises
LIMIT 51

results.question: Of accounts that were 1-30 days past due at the end of March 2026, what share had rolled to a worse bucket by the end of June 2026, by product?
results.got: For accounts that were 1-30 days past due at the end of March 2026, student lines of credit had the highest roll rate to a worse delinquency bucket by the end of June 2026 at 20.00% (2 out of 10 accounts, representing a small sample). Among higher-volume products, auto loans had the highest roll rate at 7.51% (37 of 493 accounts), while mortgages had the lowest at 2.83% (7 of 247 accounts). [table
sql:
WITH snaps AS (
  SELECT (SELECT max(month_end_date) FROM l2.account_monthly_snapshot WHERE CAST(month_end_date AS DATE) <= DATE '2026-03-31') AS d0,
         (SELECT max(month_end_date) FROM l2.account_monthly_snapshot WHERE CAST(month_end_date AS DATE) <= DATE '2026-06-30') AS d1
),
held AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT unnest(account_ids) AS account_id FROM l2.collections_cases WHERE insolvency_hold_flag
),
snap AS (
  SELECT account_id, month_end_date, product_type, account_status, write_off_flag,
         CASE WHEN dpd IS NULL THEN NULL WHEN dpd <= 0 THEN 'current' WHEN dpd <= 30 THEN '1-30' WHEN dpd <= 60 THEN '31-60'
              WHEN dpd <= 90 THEN '61-90' WHEN dpd <= 120 THEN '91-120' WHEN dpd <= 150 THEN '121-150'
              WHEN dpd <= 180 THEN '151-180' ELSE '180+' END AS bucket
  FROM l2.account_monthly_snapshot
)
SELECT a.product_type AS product, 
       count(*) FILTER (WHERE list_position(['current', '1-30', '31-60', '61-90', '91-120', '121-150', '151-180', '180+'], b.bucket)
                            > list_position(['current', '1-30', '31-60', '61-90', '91-120', '121-150', '151-180', '180+'], a.bucket)) AS numerator,
       count(*) AS denominator,
       CAST(count(*) FILTER (WHERE list_position(['current', '1-30', '31-60', '61-90', '91-120', '121-150', '151-180', '180+'], b.bucket)
                                 > list_position(['current', '1-30', '31-60', '61-90', '91-120', '121-150', '151-180', '180+'], a.bucket)) AS DOUBLE)
         / nullif(count(*), 0) AS value
FROM snaps
JOIN snap a ON a.month_end_date = snaps.d0
LEFT JOIN snap b ON b.account_id = a.account_id AND b.month_end_date = snaps.d1
WHERE snaps.d1 > snaps.d0
  AND a.bucket IS NOT NULL
  AND NOT coalesce(a.write_off_flag, false)
  AND coalesce(a.account_status, '') <> 'charged_off'
  AND a.account_id NOT IN (SELECT account_id FROM held WHERE account_id IS NOT NULL)
  AND a.bucket = '1-30'
GROUP BY ALL
ORDER BY value DESC NULLS LAST, product
LIMIT 51

answer.answer_text: For accounts that were 1-30 days past due at the end of March 2026, student lines of credit had the highest roll rate to a worse delinquency bucket by the end of June 2026 at 20.00% (2 out of 10 accounts, representing a small sample). Among higher-volume products, auto loans had the highest roll rate at 7.51% (37 of 493 accounts), while mortgages had the lowest at 2.83% (7 of 247 accounts).
answer.insight: Auto loans rolled forward at nearly double the rate of credit cards (7.51% vs 4.41%) over the Q2 2026 snapshot period.

FROM l2.contact_history h LEFT JOIN l2.collections_cases c ON c.case_id = h.case_id
WHERE CAST(h.contact_ts_local AS DATE) BETWEEN DATE '2026-09-01' AND DATE '2026-09-30'
  AND h.is_duplicate = false
  AND h.channel <> 'system'
GROUP BY ALL
ORDER BY value DESC NULLS LAST, channel
LIMIT 51

results.question: Among randomised cases, compare the promise-kept rate of the champion strategy with challenger_A and challenger_B.

results.question: Why did outbound call volume drop on 23-24 September 2026?
results.got: Outbound call volume dropped on 23-24 September 2026 due to a severity 2 predictive dialer outage (INC-0923) that reduced call capacity by approximately 60%. Unique outbound call attempts fell from 6,945 on September 22nd to 2,880 on September 23rd and 2,953 on September 24th. Volume recovered significantly on September 25th as the backlog was addressed. answer.insight: The 58% drop in unique call attempts aligns with the 60% capacity degradation reported in incident IR-2026-0923.

results.question: What is the hardship rate of cases opened in 2026, by primary product?
results.got: In 2026, auto loans recorded the highest hardship rate among newly opened cases at 26.76%, closely followed by personal loans at 25.49% and lines of credit at 25.41%. Credit cards and overdraft cases had hardship rates of 19.82% and 18.76% respectively, while mortgages had the lowest rate at 10.68%. [table: 6 rows]
sql:
SELECT c.primary_product AS product, count(*) FILTER (WHERE c.hardship_flag) AS numerator, count(*) AS denominator, CAST(count(*) FILTER (WHERE c.hardship_flag) AS DOUBLE) / nullif(count(*), 0) AS value
FROM l2.collections_cases c
WHERE CAST(c.case_open_date AS DATE) BETWEEN DATE '2026-01-01' AND DATE '2026-12-31'
GROUP BY ALL
ORDER BY value DESC NULLS LAST, product
LIMIT 51

answer.answer_text: In 2026, auto loans recorded the highest hardship rate among newly opened cases at 26.76%, closely followed by personal loans at 25.49% and lines of credit at 25.41%. Credit cards and overdraft cases had hardship rates of 19.82% and 18.76% respectively, while mortgages had the lowest rate at 10.68%.
answer.insight: Installment loan products (auto and personal loans) and lines of credit exhibit notably higher proportions of financial hardship flags (~25–27%) than revolving credit cards (~20%) and mortgages (~11%).

results.question: How many collections cases are open today, by current bucket?
results.got: There are a total of 96,000 open collections cases today. The volume of open cases decreases as delinquency severity increases, starting with 33,639 cases in the 1-30 days past due bucket and dropping to 180 cases in the 180+ days past due bucket. [table: 7 rows]
sql:
SELECT c.current_bucket AS bucket, count(*) AS value
FROM l2.collections_cases c
WHERE CAST(c.case_open_date AS DATE) BETWEEN DATE '1900-01-01' AND DATE '2999-12-31'
  AND c.is_open
GROUP BY ALL
ORDER BY value DESC NULLS LAST, bucket
LIMIT 51

answer.answer_text: There are a total of 96,000 open collections cases today. The volume of open cases decreases as delinquency severity increases, starting with 33,639 cases in the 1-30 days past due bucket and dropping to 180 cases in the 180+ days past due bucket.
answer.insight: Over 61% of all open collections cases are in the early stages of delinquency (60 days past due or less).
